articles.title: From Plastic to Living Tissue: The Promise of Bioprinting
articles.summary: Bioprinting uses living cells and hydrogel “inks” to fabricate tissues layer by layer. Already, skin, cartilage, and blood vessel prototypes exist, and a 2025 trial printed a patient’s own cells directly onto her burns. The ultimate goal? Custom organs.

articles.title: Ötzi’s Living Legacy: Cold-Loving Yeasts Still Thrive on the Iceman
articles.summary: New research reveals that Ötzi the Iceman’s 5,300-year-old mummy hosts living, cold-adapted yeasts likely originating from the glacier. These microbes, found on his skin and in his stomach, have persisted for millennia and may have industrial potential.

articles.title: Antarctic Isolation Experiment Reveals Surprising Social Friction
articles.summary: A 10-month study at Concordia Station tracked 12 crew members with surveys and wearable sensors. Contrary to expectations, more physical proximity correlated with increased conflict, mistrust, and lower perceived performance—key insights for future Mars missions.
